in_text_mentions: The patient then sustained a fracture of the 5th right metatarsal neck and proximal phalanx of the right 5th finger at the age of 12 years old. A spine X-ray at that time also revealed reduced vertebral height at D9–D12; early superior endplate deformities in L1–L2 (Figure 6b). He then sustained a subsequent fracture of the left great toe at the age of 14 years old.

Comparative imaging (Figure 4, Figure 5 and Figure 6) highlights intrafamilial variability in skeletal involvement: mother’s advanced phalangeal resorption (Figure 4a) vs. son’s normal hand radiographs (Figure 4b); chronic vertebral deformities and scoliosis in mother (Figure 5a) vs. early biconcave fractures in son (Figure 5b); multiple compression fractures and kyphosis in mother (Figure 6a) vs. multiple mild endplate deformities in son (Figure 6b).

in_text_mentions: Lumbosacral CT revealed a comminuted fracture involving the right side of the S1 vertebral body. The fracture was associated with diffuse osteopenia, manifested by generalized decreased bone density and cortical thinning. Areas of marginal sclerosis (hyperdense condensation) surrounded the fracture site, suggesting chronic remodeling, while the remaining sacral bone displayed heterogeneous hypodensity related to severe demineralisation (Figure 5).
